text: What is the model validation interval for a systemically important institution during the transitional period?
answer: The model validation interval for a systemically important institution during the transitional period is 20 months [1]. Two versions of the same regulation, Capital Adequacy Regulation 3 v1 and v2, state the identical figure, so there is no version conflict [1][2]. The retrieved passages do not state a standard or steady state validation interval, so the difference between transitional and post transitional timing cannot be quantified here. One related timing rule sits alongside it: the model inventory review interval for the same institution type in the transitional period is also 20 months [3]. That pairing is consistent with validation outcomes being recorded in the model inventory [10]. Other retrieved material covers unrelated topics such as large exposure limits, confidence levels and backtesting, and does not bear on validation timing [1][5][6][8]. To close the gap, a source setting the ordinary validation cycle after the transitional period would be needed.
findings: Model validation for a systemically important institution must occur at least every 20 months during the transitional period [1].
The same 20 month interval appears in both v1 and v2 of the regulation, so the figure is corroborated [1][2].
The model inventory review interval for the same institution type and period is also 20 months [3].
Validation outcomes are recorded in the model inventory, which links the two intervals [10].
No retrieved passage gives the standard or post transitional validation interval, so the contrast is unresolved.

text: What is the confidence level for the internal model for a small and non-complex institution?
answer: The confidence level for the internal model for a small and non-complex institution is 96.5 % [5][6]. Both versions of Capital Adequacy Regulation 3 state the same figure, so there is no conflict to resolve [5][6]. The relevant provision is Capital Adequacy Regulation 3 Article 33, and the internal position on 96.5 % is unchanged since the last review [12]. The requirement applies at solo level from 2025-04-15 [1][2]. For context, an internal model is a model a firm uses to calculate its own regulatory figures, and a backtesting exception is measured against the confidence level [1][3]. Take care not to read across from other categories, where different quantiles apply, for example 97 % for a domestically active firm under the internal ratings based approach [17] and 99.2 % for a newly authorised firm where the exposure is unsecured [19].
